scope: Versioned trusted recovery registry: independent operation contracts, immutable source evidence, physical bounds, explicit discovery, cooperative cancellation/work budgets and legacy byte-round-trip compatibility. No synchronous CPU preemption or untrusted plugin sandbox claim.

results.name: Versioned profiles declare inspection and lossy conversion without a fictitious encoder
Registration freezes descriptors and captures trusted handlers without executing them
Executable ROM bytes are physical data and never profile registrations
Malformed descriptors cannot expose absent operations or imply inverse conversion
Duplicate registration and method-count bounds do not replace existing handlers
Discovery preserves unknown unsupported ambiguous and invalid outcomes separately
Explicit discovery selection avoids unrequested decoder work
Source-size refusal happens before any profile code is invoked
Physical identity must be bounded SHA-256 and cannot be forged by results
Evidence cannot misidentify the source or escape physical bounds
Supported recognition requires physical evidence rather than a positive label alone
Aggregate evidence range budget rejects multiplying individually valid lists
Context reads charge work and validate source provenance and exact byte ranges
Out-of-bounds context reads are refused before the physical reader runs
Cooperative method and aggregate work budgets stop further work without overcharging
Cancellation before discovery or dispatch invokes no registered code
Cancellation after a completed probe suppresses stale results and later profiles
Cooperative async checkpoints honor cancellation before returning operation data
Recognition never calls editing or conversion handlers as a side effect
Changing source identity during an async handler invalidates the operation
Malformed or oversized output is an invalid method result, not silent truncation
Shared dispatch refuses undeclared native patching without calling a handler
Legacy decode encode and explicit byte round-trip APIs retain their behavior
Legacy native encode dispatch describes only separate raw bytes and rejects unbound ranges
Shared legacy encoding rejects cross-source data, altered spans and wrong encoded lengths
Legacy discovery reports inferred applicability separately from verified decoding
A failed legacy byte round-trip remains a failure and cannot be inferred from registration
Returned evidence and operation data are frozen snapshots independent of handler objects
